items.text: Thereflector in an electricfire is a special shape,called a parabola.You can see parabolicreflectors in torches andradio telescopes,for example.

items.label: text
items.text: Whenyou turnon abathroom heater,asshown inFigure 15.9,youwill feel theeffect almost instantly.Neitherconduction norconvection can explain how heatisgetting from the hotpart toyourhands.Conduction doesnot occur that rapidly,eveningood thermal conductors,and airisapoor thermal conductor. Convectionresultsinheated airfloating upwards on colder,denser air.

items.label: text
items.text: There aretwo thingsyou shouldnotice about this example.

items.label: list_item
items.text: 1Theheat thatyoufeel soquickly is travelling from theheater ina straight line.

items.label: list_item
items.text: 2Thedesign of thebathroom heaterincludes a specially shaped,very shiny reflector,similar to the reflectorbehind a fluorescent light or in a torch.

items.label: text
items.text: In thisexample,heat is travelling in the form ofwaves,likevisiblelight. Heatwaves are called infrared (IR)waves or IRradiation.The army and the emergency services use special cameras,called thermal imaging cameras, that can detect objectsgiving out IRwaves.These cameras show images of people because of the heatradiation from theirbodies,even when there isnot enoughvisible light to actually see them.Thermal imaging isalso an important tool in the diagnosis of certain illnesses.（Figure 15.10)

items.label: text
items.text: Figure 15.10 This is a thermal image of a patient showing areas of different temperatures.

items.label: text
items.text: IRwaves arepart of the samefamilyofwavesaslight,radiowaves,ultraviolet and so on,called the electromagnetic（EM) spectrum (seepage 106).IRwaves, Inparticular,IRcan travel through avacuum and doessoat the speed of light (3x108m/s).

items.label: text
items.text: It isimportant thatheat can travel in thisway,without the need formatter, otherwise we wouldnotreceive heat,aswell aslight,from the Sun.

items.label: text
items.text: IRwavescan alsobereflected and absorbedby different materials,just like visible light.Highlypolished,shiny surfaces aregood reflectors of thermal radiation.White surfaces alsoreflect alot of IR.Matt (not shiny)black and dark surfaces arepoorreflectors or,toput it more positively,are good absorbers of heatradiation.Figure 15.12 shows how this canbe useful in everyday life
